title: Caregiver Oral Reading Prosody Is Associated With Preschoolers' Storybook Listening Comprehension.
abstract: Shared reading is one of the most language-enriched contexts in children's home environments. A salient, understudied characteristic of shared reading is caregiver oral reading prosody. While caregiver prosody in conversational contexts is linked to children's understanding of spoken language, it remains unclear whether caregivers' oral reading prosody relates to preschoolers' storybook listening comprehension. The present study examined caregiver oral reading prosody in relation to preschool-age children's listening comprehension of book text. Thirty-eight caregivers read a children's book to their child (ages: 4-5 years) without extratextual discussion. Children then answered cued recall questions about the story and were assessed on broader listening comprehension skills via standardized assessment.
